get.description: One row per admin write (#313 Tasks 1-2), newest first by ActionUtc then Id (a tiebreaker: many rows from the same write batch can share one ActionUtc instant). EntityType and EntityId together answer 'history of this row'; ActorId and Action narrow by who/what — ActorId matches case-insensitively, EntityType does not. FromUtc/ToUtc bound the range and are both inclusive; pass an explicit time-of-day, since a date alone (e.g. toUtc=2026-09-02) means midnight at the start of that day and so excludes everything that happened on it. All filters are optional and combine with AND. EntityId is null on a create of an entity with a store-generated key (the database assigns it during the very write this row records, so it does not exist yet) — such a row can never be found through the EntityId filter and is identified through its After payload instead, which holds the created entity's full property set.

Proxies GitHub's run list for the CI workflow (GitHub:Workflow, default ci.yml), newest first. Optional 'branch' filters to one branch; 'limit' is 1–50, default 20. Cached for 60 seconds. Test counts are not part of a run: read them from GET /admin/ci/runs/{id}/tests. 503 when GitHub:Token is not set.

Reads the test-results.json from the run's test-results artifact: totals, then each test project with every test's outcome, duration and failure message. 404 when the run doesn't exist, has no report (still running, or stopped before its tests reported), or its report has expired. Cached by artifact, since an artifact never changes. 503 when GitHub:Token is not set.

get.summary: List every table the admin data browser can read
get.description: Slug, display name and current row count for each table registered in BrowsableTables.

get.summary: Read one browsable table's rows, masked and paginated
get.description: Strictly read-only. Every column SensitiveProperties marks sensitive is replaced with "<redacted>" server-side before this response is built — the full value never leaves the API from this endpoint (a full reveal, audited, is a separate future endpoint). 'sort' is a column name, optionally prefixed with '-' for descending (e.g. sort=-CreatedUtc); paging is stable even without an explicit sort, via an always-appended primary-key tiebreaker. 'filter' is 'column:value' — exact match for a non-string column, case-insensitive contains for a string column, split on the first ':' only so a value such as an ISO-8601 timestamp can itself contain colons. Both 'sort' and 'filter' column names are matched case-sensitively (e.g. 'CreatedUtc', not 'createdUtc') against the table's exposed-column whitelist and rejected with 400 if unknown, wrong-case or sensitive — a sensitive column would otherwise let a filter be used to guess a masked value one character at a time.

post.description: The escape hatch around the data browser's server-side masking (#315). Only a column registered in SensitiveProperties for the table's entity may be revealed — any other column, including an already-unmasked one, is a 400. Every successful reveal writes an admin_audit_log row (Action=Reveal) recording who revealed which column on which row and when; Before/After are never populated and the value itself never appears in the row, only its column name. The audit row is committed before this response is returned — a failed audit write fails the whole request with a 500 rather than returning a value with no audit trail. Responses carry Cache-Control: no-store. Rate-limited per actor (RateLimiting:AdminReveal), far tighter than the rest of the admin API: this endpoint exists to be used rarely, not as a second browsing mode.

get.description: Returns the flight with its current status and its 50 most recent status events, newest first — the record of what the sync actually saw. Not the full history: a long-tracked flight polled every couple of minutes accumulates status-event rows without bound. StatusHistoryTruncated is true when the cap actually cut rows off; when it is, see GET /admin/data/flight-status-events for the rest.

Runs every registered health check with no predicate — including 'aeroapi' and 'apns', tagged 'external' and excluded from the load-balancer probe at /health/ready — and always responds 200, even when the overall status is Unhealthy. Also reports process/build info (version, build SHA, uptime), pending EF Core migrations, and the flight-status sync's last-run heartbeat. Exception detail on individual checks and the sync's last error render outside Production only.

get.description: Returns the traveler together with its device tokens, tracked flights and loyalty memberships in one call. Email and every device token are masked as "<redacted>"; reveal the real value via POST /admin/data/{table}/{id}/reveal. TrackedFlights is capped at 50, newest first; TrackedFlightsTruncated is true when the cap actually cut rows off, and the full relationship is available via GET /admin/data/traveler-flights. Device tokens and loyalty memberships are not capped.

Returns every traveler, paged. Email is masked as "<redacted>"; reveal the real value via POST /admin/data/travelers/{id}/reveal, which audits the read. This is the intended posture, not a gap to be fixed back.

Returns one traveler. Email is masked as "<redacted>"; reveal the real value via POST /admin/data/travelers/{id}/reveal, which audits the read. This is the intended posture, not a gap to be fixed back.

delete.description: Removes a stale APNs device token. This is NOT a device revocation: it only stops push notifications from reaching that token, and the client re-registers a fresh one on its next launch.

get.description: Proxies FlightAware's own GET /account/usage report — calls, pages and cost for the range, broken down by operation, alongside the configured monthly budget and the next available outbound throttle slot. Optional 'start' and 'end' are UTC instants; they default to the current UTC month to date. AeroAPI serves at most one year of history, so an earlier start is rejected. Cached for 10 minutes, matching FlightAware's own refresh cadence.

get.summary: Search flights by route or flight number on a date
get.description:
Searches scheduled flights to populate the 'add flight' picker. Each returned row has exactly the same shape as TrackFlightRequest (flightNumber, serviceDate, departureAirportIata, arrivalAirportIata, scheduledDepartureUtc, scheduledArrivalUtc), so a result can be posted straight to POST /flights, unmodified, to track it.

Search criteria (query params):
- date (required): the departure date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Must fall within the provider's rolling past/future horizon.
- from / to (optional): departure and arrival airport as 3-letter IATA codes (e.g. LHR, JFK). Case-insensitive. Must be supplied together.
- flightNumber (optional): an IATA flight code — a 2-character airline prefix containing at least one letter, followed by 1–4 digits and an optional trailing letter (e.g. BA123, 6E4120, BA123A). Case-insensitive. The same rule POST /flights applies, so any flightNumber this endpoint accepts is trackable.
- includeCodeshares (optional, default false): when true, includes codeshare-marketed rows for the same physical departure alongside the operating flight's own row; when false, only the operating flight's own row is returned.

You must provide either a full route (both from and to) OR a flightNumber, in addition to date; otherwise the request is rejected with 400.

Each result is one flight designator — the same aircraft sold under several marketing numbers (e.g. TK1028 is also 6E4120, MS9668, RJ3710 and SQ6228) appears as one row per number, not grouped. There is no separate 'operating carrier' field: the airline is always the first two characters of the result's own flightNumber.

Responses:
- 200: list of matching flights (empty list when the provider responds successfully but nothing matches).
- 400: invalid/insufficient parameters.
- 500: server-side configuration issue with the flight data provider.
- 502: the flight data provider was unreachable or returned an unexpected error.
- 503: the flight data provider is throttling requests; retry after the period in the Retry-After header.
Returns a paginated list of flights the authenticated traveler is tracking. Supports ?page and ?pageSize (default 50, max 200).

post.description: Adds a flight to the authenticated traveler's tracking list. A row returned by GET /flights/search can be posted here unmodified — this body is exactly that shape. If the flight already exists in the system (same airline, number, and service date) it is reused; otherwise a new flight record is created. The airline is derived from the first two characters of FlightNumber (e.g. 'BA123' -> 'BA', '6E4120' -> '6E'); there is no separate airline field. Body fields: FlightNumber (e.g. 'BA123' or '6E4120'), ServiceDate (YYYY-MM-DD), DepartureAirportIata, ArrivalAirportIata, ScheduledDepartureUtc, ScheduledArrivalUtc.

delete.description: Removes the specified flight from the authenticated traveler's tracking list. Route parameter: flightId — the numeric ID returned when the flight was tracked.

patch.description: Enables or disables push notifications for a tracked flight. Route parameter: flightId — the numeric flight ID. Body: { "notify": true } (true to enable, false to disable). Notifications are delivered via APNs to device tokens registered for the traveler.

get.description: Returns the ordered list of status events recorded for the flight. Each event captures the status code, gate/terminal info, baggage claim, and the time it became effective. Route parameter: flightId — the numeric flight ID.

post.description: Triggers an on-demand status refresh for the specified flight by querying the external flight data provider. Returns { updated: true } if new status data was fetched and persisted, or { updated: false } if the data was already up to date. Route parameter: flightId — the numeric flight ID.

get.description: Returns all lounges at the specified airport, each annotated with whether the authenticated traveler is eligible to access it. Eligibility is computed from the traveler's loyalty memberships and tier benefits. Query parameter: airportIata — the IATA airport code (e.g. 'LHR', 'JFK').
Returns loyalty programs linked to the specified airline IATA code (e.g. 'BA'). Use this to populate the program picker when the user knows their airline.
Returns a paginated list of airline loyalty programs, including their full tier hierarchy. Use this to populate program/tier picker UIs. Supports ?page and ?pageSize (default 50, max 200).
Returns a paginated list of the authenticated traveler's loyalty memberships. Supports ?page and ?pageSize (default 50, max 200).

post.description: Links a loyalty program membership to the authenticated traveler. Body fields: ProgramId (from GET /loyalty/programs), AccountNumber, TierId (optional, from the program's tier list), TierExpiryDate (optional, YYYY-MM-DD), PointsExpiryDate (optional, YYYY-MM-DD).

put.description: Replaces the account number, tier, and expiry dates for the specified membership. Route parameter: id — the membership ID returned when it was added. Only the authenticated traveler's own memberships can be updated.

delete.description: Deletes a loyalty membership from the authenticated traveler's profile. Route parameter: id — the membership ID to remove.

post.description: Creates a traveler profile linked to the authenticated Azure AD B2C identity. Idempotent — safe to call on every login; does nothing if the traveler already exists.

get.description: Returns the authenticated traveler's profile. Display name is owned by Azure AD B2C and is refreshed from the sign-in token on each login; it is read-only here.

post.description: Registers a push notification device token for the authenticated traveler. Currently supports iOS (APNs). The token is used to send flight status alerts when notifications are enabled for a tracked flight.

get.description: Returns all push notification device tokens registered for the authenticated traveler.

delete.description: Removes a previously registered push notification device token. Use this when a user logs out or when the OS invalidates the token. Route parameter: deviceTokenId — the ID of the device token to remove.

Bearer.description: Enter 'Bearer' followed by a space and the JWT.
